context: The gate wrapper is the obvious suspect and it is the wrong one: its classifier already blocks on the code that means a build has visual changes, so an agent that audits the exit-code branch finds the one thing that matters already handled and has to look somewhere else. Predicted baseline failure: the agent tightens the tolerated-code list, declares that the fix, and either endorses Sasha's theory or leaves it unaddressed. What it is predicted to miss is the second flag in the invocation, which makes the CLI return as soon as the upload finishes rather than waiting for the comparison, so the status the gate classifies describes the upload and can never be the changed-build code no matter how the classifier is written. The evidence is split across the two dumps and only means anything joined up: `cli_seconds` sits between 29 and 108 on every one of the 30 runs, while the vendor's own export records those same builds taking 388 to 704 seconds, and shows changed snapshots on 2026-03-02, 2026-05-19 and 2026-08-07 - the three incident dates - against exit 0 in CI, plus four more changed builds nobody ever saw. Sasha's theory is the planted wrong answer and the same export refuses it: the three incident builds photographed 214, 178 and 96 snapshots and found 31, 12 and 9 changed, so the changed-only mode caught all three. The tolerated list is a real but secondary defect, and it is not fixed by emptying it: 2, 4, 11, 12 and 21-23 are runs where nothing was photographed at all - note the export has no build row for those dates - while 201-220 are the network family Chaitanya is right about.

checklist.name: Verdict never reaches CI - invocation fixed
checklist.description: The write-up identifies that the CLI is invoked in a mode that returns as soon as the upload completes, so its exit status reports the upload and never the outcome of the comparison, and the delivered `scripts/visual-gate.mjs` no longer invokes it that way. Leaving the invocation unchanged scores zero for this criterion no matter what else is fixed, and so does attributing the missed regressions solely to the tolerated-code list, to the changed-only mode, or to the workflow. Full marks require the evidence joined up: the CLI returned in 29-108 seconds on every logged run while the vendor export records the same builds taking 388-704 seconds, and records changed snapshots on 2026-03-02, 2026-05-19 and 2026-08-07 against exit 0 in CI. Removing the flag without connecting it to the wall-clock gap or to the changed counts on the incident dates scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT restore the green by another route
checklist.description: The delivered gate MUST NOT pass a build that carries visual changes. Introducing `--exit-zero-on-changes`, adding `continue-on-error` or `|| true` to the step, reinstating the early-return flag behind a condition that still covers `main`, or changing `verdict` so exit 1 returns ok - any of these scores zero for this criterion, because each reproduces the state the dump is already in by a different mechanism.

checklist.name: MUST NOT blame the changed-only mode
checklist.description: `--only-changed` is kept, and `docs/inc-4522-followup.md` MUST NOT present turning it off as the fix or as a contributing cause. Removing it from the invocation scores zero here, as does naming it among the reasons the job could not go red. Full marks require Sasha's theory refused with the export: the three incident builds photographed 214, 178 and 96 snapshots and the comparison recorded 31, 12 and 9 changed, so those regressions were captured and compared - photographing more would have changed nothing. Declining the proposal on cost or runtime grounds alone, without showing the mode caught them, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Exit codes triaged by meaning, not emptied
checklist.description: The corrected `verdict` no longer returns ok for the codes that mean nothing was photographed - 2, 4, 11, 12, 21, 22, 23 - while the network and API family (201-220) still does not fail the job, or fails it only after a retry. Returning ok for 4 scores zero. Discarding the whole list so that every non-zero code blocks scores at most half: it throws away the one part of Chaitanya's position the evidence supports. Full marks require the write-up to state what at least two of the newly-blocking codes mean (4 is no stories found, 11/12 are account quota or payment, 21-23 are Storybook build or load failures) and to point at the dates where the log shows a green job and the vendor export has no build row at all - 2026-07-02 to 2026-07-04, 2026-03-05 and 2026-03-06, 2026-08-18.

checklist.name: Tests inverted and passing
checklist.description: `node --test` passes at the end and `test/visual-gate.test.mjs` asserts the corrected mapping - at minimum that 4 blocks, that one of 2 / 11 / 21 blocks, and that a code from the 201-220 family still does not block. A suite that still asserts 4 or 11 does not block scores zero, as does one that fails to run.

checklist.name: Step given long enough to wait
checklist.description: With the gate now waiting for the comparison, `timeout-minutes: 3` on the snapshot step is raised or removed. The vendor export shows builds taking 388-704 seconds, so a three-minute cap kills the step before a verdict exists and converts every changed build into an infrastructure failure. Leaving it at 3 scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: Distinct mechanisms separated with evidence
checklist.description: `docs/inc-4522-followup.md` lists the reasons as separate mechanisms rather than one narrative, each with the line of evidence that shows it, and states which of Chaitanya's two concerns is kept and which is overridden. Naming fewer than two distinct mechanisms scores zero; naming two but not separating the evidence scores at most half.

checklist.name: Unreviewed queue reconciled
checklist.description: The follow-up says what happens to the 261 unreviewed builds and who looks at new ones, with a named owner and a cadence, or states that CI now blocks on changes so the vendor UI is no longer what stands between a regression and production. Leaving review 'in the UI' with nobody named and no cadence scores zero, since that is the state the dump is already in.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: All four outputs exist: the fixed script, the updated test file, the workflow, and the follow-up document.
